newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs hit by strong industrial data.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs hit by strong industrial data.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures were weaker but kept their composure despite a drop in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures on Tuesday following the release of stronger-than-expected industrial output data.

Japan's Trade Ministry said the country's industrial production rose a preliminary 1.0 percent in September from the previous month. It also forecast a four percent month-on-month increase in manufacturers' output for October.
Dealers said the yen's persistent weakness against the dollar and high-yielding currencies also contributed to declines across the Japanese yield curve.

June Euroyen was quoted one tick above its intra-day low of 99.24 in late trade against an IMM close at 99.27. December JGBs fell to a low of 124.25 before recovering to close at 124.34 against their opening 124.60.

"Euroyen tried to follow the JGB move but the production numbers were not strong enough to convince the market the Bank of Japan would change its monetary policy," said a Japanese bank dealer, adding that June Euroyen would need to close below 99.24 on Wednesday to head lower.
"We'll need something more than the industrial production numbers to convince people the market is going down," he said.
Dealers said the September Euroyen contract saw unusual interest because June's level was too close to the cash market to allow it to track the long end of the yield curve.
They said an early comment by Finance Minister Wataru Kubo about Japan not needing to formulate an extra stimulative budget for the current fiscal year gave JGBs an initial boost.
Eurodollar futures ended slightly easier ahead of the third quarter U.S. employment cost index, due at 1330 GMT, which is expected to show a 0.8 percent rise.
But dealers said the market was likely to pay more attention to the non-farm payrolls report for October, expected on Friday.
March Eurodollars ended at 94.30 against their IMM close at 94.30 on turnover of a mere 2,115 lots.
